cohort: The study included 560 pregnant women undergoing either elective or emergency lower segment cesarean sections (LSCS) at the Government Maternity Hospital, Tirupati.
finding: Emergency LSCS is significantly associated with a higher incidence of surgical site infections (8.2%) compared to elective LSCS (1.07%), with risk factors like postoperative anemia and obesity being more prevalent in emergency cases.
mod_finding: Emergency lower segment cesarean sections showed a significantly higher incidence of surgical site infections (8.2%) compared to elective procedures (1.07%).
